story.head: The Islanders roll four lines, the Jets lean on their top six
paras: The Jets won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-3 in overtime in Winnipeg on Nov 19. The Islanders (12-7-5) beat St. Louis 3-2 in a shootout on Wednesday, and the Jets have won two in a row. Going in, the Jets are fifth in the Central (14th in the NHL) and the Islanders third in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th).

The Jets’ record (.577) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.503), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Islanders’ (.604 on chances worth .511), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Jets create more chances on the penalty kill than almost anyone (3rd) and pick their shots (3rd lowest), but have a leaky penalty kill (29th). The Islanders have had the league’s best goaltending (1st) and get their defensemen shooting (2nd). The Isles roll four lines, but the Jets lean on their top six.

Kyle Connor (20 G / 15 A / 35 P in 26 GP) leads the Jets in scoring and is fifth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and a point in five straight games against the Islanders. Mark Scheifele (9 G / 24 A / 33 P in 26 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 17 A / 26 P in 24 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Simon Holmström (10 G / 8 A / 18 P in 24 GP) has a team-high ten goals.
Stuart Skinner (8-5-4 / .887 SV% in 18 GS) is expected to start for Winnipeg, and Semyon Varlamov (2-2-3 / .888 SV% in 7 GS) for the Islanders.
